subsystems.name: Photometric instrument
subsystems.role: records the tiny dip in starlight as a planet crosses its star.
parts: fine guidance sensors for stable pointing

subsystems.name: Data reduction pipeline
subsystems.role: turns raw images into clean light curves.

subsystems.name: Transit fitting
subsystems.role: measures the centre time and duration of each transit precisely.

subsystems.name: Signal search
subsystems.role: looks for periodic offsets in transit times or durations caused by a moon.

subsystems.name: False-positive vetting
subsystems.role: rules out other explanations for the signal.

subsystems.name: Follow-up observations
subsystems.role: uses other telescopes to confirm or refute a candidate.

buildSteps.title: Choose target systems
buildSteps.detail: Select transiting planets with many recorded transits and long observation baselines, because a moon's signal accumulates over time.

buildSteps.title: Obtain high-precision photometry
buildSteps.detail: Collect continuous, high-cadence light curves from space telescopes to reach the parts-per-million precision needed.

buildSteps.title: Correct instrument and stellar noise
buildSteps.detail: Remove spacecraft pointing drifts, detector systematics and the star's own brightness variations.

buildSteps.title: Measure transit times and durations
buildSteps.detail: Fit each transit to find its mid-point and length, then compile the series of variations.

buildSteps.title: Search for periodic signals
buildSteps.detail: Apply periodograms or Bayesian model comparison to detect small, repeating offsets in timing or duration.

buildSteps.title: Test against false positives
buildSteps.detail: Run injection-recovery tests and check whether stellar activity, a second planet, or a background binary could mimic the signal.

buildSteps.title: Model the planet–moon dynamics
buildSteps.detail: Simulate the gravitational interaction to see if a stable moon orbit reproduces the observed variations.

buildSteps.title: Follow up with other telescopes
buildSteps.detail: Schedule additional transits with Hubble, JWST or CHEOPS to see if the signal repeats and holds up.

buildSteps.title: Validate or set limits
buildSteps.detail: Combine all evidence to either claim a detection or publish an upper limit on moon size in that system.

prerequisites.why: instruments like Kepler, TESS and CHEOPS can detect the tiny brightness changes involved.
transit timing variations grow over many orbits, so years of data are needed.
N-body simulations predict which signals are physically possible and stable.
several stellar and instrumental effects can imitate transit timing signals.
PLATO and JWST offer the precision and cadence to confirm candidates, but are not yet fully exploited.

pathway.milestone: Reanalysis of Kepler and TESS data; candidate signals around gas giants such as Kepler-1625b and Kepler-1708b remain disputed
pathway.unlocks: proven methodology and published upper limits.

pathway.milestone: JWST and CHEOPS follow-up of the best candidate systems
pathway.unlocks: confirmation or refutation of existing exomoon claims.

pathway.milestone: PLATO's long, uninterrupted stares at bright stars
pathway.unlocks: a systematic survey capable of finding the first confirmed exomoon.

pathway.milestone: Dedicated space telescopes or extremely large ground observatories with high-contrast imaging
pathway.unlocks: direct study of exomoons and their atmospheres.
